content: To effectively separate priorities, a systematic approach should be employed when conducting a research priority-setting exercise. This process involves clear guidance for World Health Organization (WHO) staff. Phase 3: Publish At this stage, it is essential to develop a comprehensive publication and dissemination plan. A publication and dissemination strategy should include detailed reporting on the following aspects: Objectives of the research; Context in which the research is conducted; Methods used to identify priorities; The specific research priorities identified; The implementation plan for these priorities; and The monitoring and evaluation plan to track progress. Annex 1: A Systematic Approach to Research Priority-Setting Phase 4: Typically, this involves assessing improvements in public health outcomes. These improvements can be evaluated through metrics such as increased awareness, uptake, implementation, translation, and the overall impact of the research priorities.
